extracted.intended_audience: LaTeX users writing graphics with the pgf/TikZ package (authors creating diagrams/nodes/shadings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and options for creating shadings, establishing bounding boxes, clipping, and defining/placing nodes and edges in pgf/TikZ pictures.

rubrics_metrics.name: shading angle
rubrics_metrics.description: shading angle=(angle) — rotates the shading (not the path!) by the given angle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: turn a top-to-bottom axis shading into left-to-right by rotating 90°. The rotation affects the shading orientation but not the path geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: top color (axis shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: top color=(color) — prescribes the color used at the top in an axis shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When given: (1) the shade option is selected; (2) shading=axis is selected; (3) the middle color is set to the average of the given top color and the current bottom color; (4) the rotation angle of the shading is set to 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: bottom color (axis shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: bottom color=(color) — same as top color but for the bottom of an axis shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Behaves analogously to top color (selects shade and shading=axis, affects middle color).

rubrics_metrics.name: middle color (axis shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: middle color=(color) — specifies the color for the middle of an axis shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets shade and shading=axis, but does not change the rotation angle. Note: since top color and bottom color change the middle color, give middle color last if setting all three.

rubrics_metrics.name: left/right color (axis shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: left color=(color) / right color=(color) — like top/right but sets the shading angle to 90°.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selects appropriate axis shading and sets rotation angle so left/right correspond to axis orientation.

rubrics_metrics.name: inner color (radial shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: inner color=(color) — sets the color used at the center of a radial shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When used, shade and shading=radial options are set automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: outer color (radial shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: outer color=(color) — sets the color used at the border and outside of a radial shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use together with inner color to control radial gradients.

rubrics_metrics.name: ball color (ball shading)
rubrics_metrics.description: ball color=(color) — sets the color used for the ball shading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets shade and shading=ball. Note: the ball will never be completely that color — highlights mix in white, borders mix black. ball color=white or ball color=black are meaningful choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: use as bounding box / \useasboundingbox
rubrics_metrics.description: use as bounding box option (or \useasboundingbox shorthand) — use the bounding box of the present path to determine picture size; subsequent paths are ignored for picture size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effectively tells pgf to treat subsequent drawing as if clipped for sizing purposes (without actual clipping). If previous operations established a larger bounding box it will not be reduced. When used inside a scope the effect lasts until the end of the scope. Useful for overlapping the main text, and for controlling whitespace around the picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: current bounding box node
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'current bounding box' node to get the size of the current bounding box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The current bounding box node has rectangle shape and its size is the current bounding box; likewise current path bounding box returns size of current path bounding box — useful for drawing frames around the computed box.

rubrics_metrics.name: clip option and \clip command
rubrics_metrics.description: clip — causes all subsequent drawings to be clipped against the current path; \clip is shorthand for \path[clip].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clipping makes size of subsequent paths irrelevant for picture size. For self-intersecting paths the even-odd rule or nonzero winding number rule is used to determine inside/outside. The clipping path is a graphic state parameter and resets at end of scope; multiple clippings accumulate (intersection). It is usually best to apply clip only to the first path command in a scope. You cannot specify certain graphic options for the command used for clipping (e.g., moving fill=red into the clipped command may fail); avoid specifying options on clipping commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: localize clipping with scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Use {scope} environments to keep clipping local to a region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ending a scope is the only way to enlarge the clipping area previously restricted by clip operations; encapsulate clip operations in a scope to avoid affecting the whole picture.

rubrics_metrics.name: node operation and placement basics
rubrics_metrics.description: node — nodes are added to paths using the node path operation; nodes are not part of the path but are placed after the path is drawn and thus drawn on top of the path.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Node syntax: \path ... node[options](name) at (coordinate) {text} ... ; 'at' places the node at the given coordinate rather than the current path position. Multiple nodes on a path are drawn in the order encountered. Nodes can have borders/backgrounds or be shape-only without text.

rubrics_metrics.name: node name option
rubrics_metrics.description: name=(node name) or (name) — assigns a name to the node for later reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-level names may contain spaces, numbers, letters; avoid punctuation like dot/comma/colon since these are used for coordinate parsing. The explicit (name) syntax and the name= option are equivalent.

rubrics_metrics.name: at=(coordinate) alternative
rubrics_metrics.description: at=(coordinate) — alternate way to place a node at a specific coordinate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Functionally similar to 'at' in the node syntax; not available when the node is inside a path operation (would not make sense).

rubrics_metrics.name: node-local options vs outside options
rubrics_metrics.description: The (options) in node[...] apply only to the node; many outside options also apply to nodes but some do not (e.g., outside rotation does not apply to nodes unless special options are used).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outside path actions like draw or fill never apply to the node automatically and must be given inside the node options (unless special options are used).

rubrics_metrics.name: shape selection for nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: shape=(shape name) or simply specifying a shape option (e.g., circle) — selects the node shape (default is rectangle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TikZ will interpret an unknown option as a shape name if other checks fail. Standard shapes: rectangle, circle, coordinate; ellipse if pgflibraryshapes is loaded. Shapes define anchors and size options discussed elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: style=every node and style=every <shape> node
rubrics_metrics.description: style=every node and style=every (shape) node — styles installed at the beginning of every node or every node of a given shape.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these styles to globally affect rendering of all nodes or all nodes of a particular shape (e.g., \tikzstyle{every node}=[draw]).

rubrics_metrics.name: light-weight nodes: coordinate
rubrics_metrics.description: coordinate[...] (or \coordinate) — a light-weight 'node' with shape=coordinate and empty text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to node[shape=coordinate]{}; useful for storing coordinates without typesetting node text.

rubrics_metrics.name: multi-part nodes and \nodepart
rubrics_metrics.description: \nodepart{part name} — used inside a node's text argument to create multipart nodes (shapes define which parts exist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stops typesetting the current part and begins typesetting the named part until another \nodepart or the node ends. Styles every <part> node part apply to node parts (e.g., every lower node part). Useful for shapes like 'circle split' or UML/class boxes.

rubrics_metrics.name: text color and text opacity in nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: text=(color) sets the text color in nodes; text opacity=(value) sets opacity for node text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A later color= option will override text=. Text opacity controls only the text; fill/draw opacity are controlled separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: font option for node text
rubrics_metrics.description: font=(font commands) — sets the font used for text labels inside a node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used inline or via styles such as every text node part to set fonts for specific node parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: text width and automatic line breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: text width=(dimension) — put node text in a box of the given width (a minipage); if text is larger it will be line-broken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default text width uses a right-ragged border (no full justification). For narrow nodes this avoids ugly justification. Use text justified to request full justification (for broader nodes).

rubrics_metrics.name: text justified / text ragged / text badly ragged
rubrics_metrics.description: text justified — justify lines; text ragged — LATEX-style balanced ragged-right (default when text width set); text badly ragged — LATEX-style ragged without balancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: text ragged balances the right border; text badly ragged avoids balancing and hyphenation and may be useful for very narrow boxes. text justified should be used only with pretty broad nodes (otherwise lines may be badly set).

rubrics_metrics.name: text centered / text badly centered
rubrics_metrics.description: text centered — center text with balancing; text badly centered — center without balancing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when centered multi-line nodes are desired; badly centered may be useful for narrow nodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: minimum height / text height / text depth
rubrics_metrics.description: minimum height=(dimension) ensures whole node height at least given height; text height=(dimension) sets the height of the text box used to determine node size; text depth sets the depth of the text box.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text height replaces the natural typeset height of the text box (and inner sep + depth still apply). The author recommends using minimum size instead of text height except for special situations. text depth is useful for aligning nodes with uniform depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: anchor placement
rubrics_metrics.description: anchor=(anchor name) — shift the node so the named anchor lies on the current coordinate (default anchor is center).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchors include compass directions (north, south, east, west etc.), center, base, base west/east, mid/mid west/mid east for vertical centering relative to 'x' height. Note that to place a node visually above a point you typically use anchor=south (counterintuitive), so helper options exist (above, left, right, below) mapping to appropriate anchors.

rubrics_metrics.name: intuitive directional shortcuts: above/left/right/below and offsets
rubrics_metrics.description: above=(offset), above left=(offset), above right=(offset), left=(offset), right=(offset), below=(offset), below left=(offset), below right=(offset) — map to specific anchors and optionally shift by offset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: above = anchor=south; above left = anchor=south east; above right = anchor=south west; left = anchor=east; right = anchor=west; behavior matches anchors but uses offset to add separation (e.g., above=2pt).

rubrics_metrics.name: relative placement: above of / left of / right of / below of / ...
rubrics_metrics.description: above of=(node) / above left of=(node) / above right of=(node) / left of / right of / below of / below left of / below right of — place current node relative to another named node at distance node distance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The node is placed at the distance node distance from the named node; the anchor used is center (unless other anchors/options specified). The node distance is Euclidean distance between centers, not L1.

rubrics_metrics.name: node distance
rubrics_metrics.description: node distance=(dimension) — sets the distance used by the '... of' relative placement options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distance is between centers of nodes (not between borders). Useful to globally control spacing when placing nodes relative to others.

rubrics_metrics.name: transformations and transform shape
rubrics_metrics.description: By default transformations do not apply to nodes (to avoid scaling/rotating text). transform shape causes the external transformation matrix to be applied to the node shape; giving transformation options inside the node option list applies those transformations to the node.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transform shape if you want node shapes/text scaled by e.g. \tikz[scale=3]. Inline rotate/scale options inside a node always apply to that node (e.g., node[rotate=90,scale=1.5]).

rubrics_metrics.name: pos option for placing nodes on a path
rubrics_metrics.description: pos=(fraction) — places a node anchored on the line/curve from the previous coordinate to the current point at the given fractional 'time' or position (0 = previous, 1 = current).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For straight -- lines a fraction is proportional to linear distance (0.5 is middle). For .. curves pos=0.5 is the parameter time 0.5 (not necessarily midpoint by arc length). For |- and -| the position 0.5 equals the corner. pos currently does not work for some path construction operations (e.g., arcs may not be supported yet).

rubrics_metrics.name: auto placement and swap
rubrics_metrics.description: auto=(left|right|false) — automatically choose an anchor (left or right of the line) for nodes placed on lines/curves; swap exchanges left and right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leaving out the direction enables auto placement with last left/right value; auto=false disables automatic placement. Auto is overridden by explicit anchor or above/below options. swap toggles left/right behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: sloped and allow upside down
rubrics_metrics.description: sloped — rotate the node so a horizontal line becomes tangent to the curve (align with slope). allow upside down=(true|false) — whether to allow upside-down text when sloped is used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By default sloped rotates but keeps text 'right side up'; set allow upside down=true or use rotate=180 to get upside-down text. Useful for labeling curved/angled edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: positioning shorthand styles (midway, near start/end, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: midway, near start, near end, very near start, very near end, at start, at end — predefined styles for pos fractions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: midway = pos=0.5; near start = pos=0.25; near end = pos=0.75; very near start = pos=0.125; very near end = pos=0.875; at start = pos=0; at end = pos=1. Use these for concise placement of labels on paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: implicit node placement inside path operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing (0,0) -- node{a} (1,1) stores the node specification and reinserts it after the coordinate with an implicit pos value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implicitly stored node specifier has fixed catcodes at storage time (so verbatim text may not work — use a normal node after the coordinate with pos if needed). The pos value chosen for implicit nodes is inherited from the surrounding scope only for nodes specified implicitly; non-implicit nodes do not inherit that pos.

rubrics_metrics.name: label option for nodes
rubrics_metrics.description: label=[options](angle):text — adds another node (label node) placed relative to the main node according to main node.(angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The angle determines which anchor of label node is placed at main node.<angle>. Angles are mapped into discrete anchors (e.g., −3°..+3° chooses west, 4°..86° chooses south west, etc.), producing placement above/right/left/below according to angle ranges. Useful for simple attached labels without separate node commands.
